Answer: B
Reason: The ultrasound images demonstrate a multicystic mass in the fetal thorax (indicated by arrows) with visible systemic arterial supply on color Doppler, characteristic of a bronchopulmonary sequestration or CPAM. Such space-occupying lesions in the right lung typically cause mass effect, displacing the heart to the contralateral (left) side and pushing the diaphragm downward or appearing to elevate it relative to the compressed lung; among the choices, Option B best describes this significant mass effect and displacement.
